newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL MADRID AND BARCELONA MATCH TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL MADRID AND BARCELONA MATCH TACTICS.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Real Madrid and Barcelona who clash in the Spanish first division in Madrid on Saturday (kickoff 1930 GMT).

Playing style: Coach Fabio Capello uses a conventional 4-4-2 formation, but has been widely criticised for negative tactics, excessive reliance on counterattacks, and for introducing a long ball philosophy to Real. He is likely to repeat the starting line-up used in last week's game at Sporting Gijon. The only slight doubt is goalkeeper Bodo Illgner, who has been suffering from gastro-entiritis. If he fails to recover he will be replaced by Spanish international reserve Santiago Canizares.

Strengths: Goalkeeper Illgner is a tower of strength at the back, Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos moves up well to create danger down the left, while Fernando Hierro is not only the mainstay of defence but is also strong coming forward through the middle. Both Roberto Carlos, whose swirling left-foot strikes have left several goalkeepers stranded already this season, and the right-footed Hierro are superb set-piece specialists. But it is in the individual brilliance of Balkan strike pair Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic, together with that of teenager Raul Gonzalez, that Real's true strength lies.

Under Capello Real have played effectively but with little style and still don't always play well as a team. They tend to depend excessively on Mijatovic, Suker and Raul making the best of half-chances. The long-ball philosophy, which Capello denies he employs, means at times the midfield seems hardly to exist. If the game is played in midfield, Real's Victor and Redondo would be hard-pressed to match Barca's Luis Enrique and Popescu. Despite signing Illgner Real have conceded more goals from headers than any other side in the Spanish first divison.

Motivation: Real were held 1-1 at home in this fixture last autumn and will want to prove to their arch-rivals they have recovered from a disappointing 1995-96 season. A win would open up a four-point lead over the Catalans.
Line-up (probable): Bodo Illgner, Carlos Secretario, Fernando Hierro, Rafael Alkorta, Roberto Carlos, Victor Sanchez, Fernando Redondo, Clarence Seedorf, Raul Gonzalez, Davor Suker, Pedrag Mijatovic.

Playing style: Bobby Robson plays a 4-5-1 formation, in which Josep Guardiola and Gheorghe Popescu play in front of the back four to provide the link with midfield. Giovanni plays a central co-ordinating role with Ronaldo as the solitary target man.

Strengths: Barcelona's main strength can be defined in just one word, Ronaldo. The Brazilian prodigy has already scored 13 league goals, most of them after beating players with runs from well outside the area. Giovanni is another potential match-winner, while the temperamental Ivan de la Pena, who will probably not start on Saturday, is capable of coming off the bench and turning games round single-handedly. Several internationals will be sitting on the bench alongside de la Pena, and strength in depth sets Barcelona apart -- evn from Real. Weaknesses: The individual brilliance of Ronaldo has papered over inadequacies in Barcelona's teamwork. The game against Valencia -- a 3-2 victory thanks to a sensational hat-trick from the Brazilian -- showed how fragile Bobby Robson's side would be without him. Ex-Real man Luis Enrique will be under massive pressure from his former fans, who began to whistle him last year when news of his possible move to Barca was announced.

Motivation: Victory would take Barcelona back to the top of the table and compensate in part for their recent poor record in the Bernabeu stadium where they have won only one of the last ten corresponding league fixtures. Real are still undefeated in the league this campaign. Barcelona would love to be the first to conquer them. Camp Nou has for decades served as a focus for Catalan nationalism. Real Madrid epitomise centralist Spain.
Line-up (probable): Victor Baia, Albert Ferrer, Laurent Blanc, Abelardo Fernandez, Sergi Barjuan, Gheorghe Popescu, Luis Enrique Martinez, Luis Figo, Giovanni, Roger Gargia, Ronaldo
